subject: License model conversion to AWS Private Offer — approvals, billing, and evidence
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@medicorps.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medicorps.com
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Converting existing license to AWS Private Offer — procurement questions

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Procurement has a few clarifying questions before we can route a private offer through our AWS buyer instance:

1) We currently have a site-license billed annually (invoice to our central AP). For Marketplace private offers, does Redwood require the buyer to switch to usage-based billing tied to marketplace product codes, or can you mirror our existing annual invoice/PO model?

2) Approvals: our procurement team typically requires a short evidence pack for security and vendor risk (SOC 2 type II, data location, subprocessor list). Can you confirm what you provide for AWS buyers?

3) Activation timeline: once we accept a private offer in AWS, how long until the SKU is activated and our entitlement shows up for provisioning? We have a pilot start target of June 10 and need a realistic window.

4) Licensing: we sometimes convert annual licenses to a 12-month AWS private offer. Can you provide a mapping example (what Marketplace product codes map to site-license units)?

I've attached our procurement form for reference (Medicorps_Procurement_Form.pdf). If easier, would one of your finance/ops folks join a 30-minute call this week?

Thanks,
Alex Dunn
Head of Procurement
Medicorps

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@medicorps.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Converting existing license to AWS Private Offer — procurement questions

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then proposed next steps:

- Billing model: We can support both approaches. For most private offers we map the buyer PO to an annual commitment SKU in AWS (so your AP can still process a PO/invoice) — we call this a billed-commitment private offer. Usage-based private offers are also possible but not required.

- Evidence: we provide a SOC 2 Type II report, our subprocessor register, data residency statement, and an AWS Marketplace evidence bundle on request. I attached our standard PO terms (redwood_po_terms_v1.pdf) that include the summary.

- Activation timeline: Typical activation after seller-side approval is 1–3 business days for standard cases; if Finance needs manual invoice mapping or cross-org approvals it can be 3–7 business days. We'll aim for the shorter window and can push for expedited activation. See Ben's note below for the exact steps.

- Licensing mapping: we'll create a short mapping table for your SKU vs. site-license units. Can you share the licensing spreadsheet your team has? The Medico_Licensing_Summary.xlsx you mentioned in the procurement form would be perfect.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben (ops) and Neha (onboarding) join a 30-minute call Wednesday 10:00am PT to walk through the PO, activation flow, and evidence pack.
2) Alex shares the licensing spreadsheet and the internal approval cutover deadline (if any).
3) We generate a draft private offer in AWS and a DocuSign signature packet if you prefer a signed SOW before activation.

Are you available Wednesday 10:00am PT?

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

(attachment: redwood_po_terms_v1.pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@medicorps.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Converting existing license to AWS Private Offer — activation & finance routing

Alex / Aisha —

Quick note from Seller Operations:

Activation & finance checklist (high level):
- Seller drafts the Private Offer in AWS and includes the annual-commitment SKU + custom price.
- We send the offer to the buyer account (your procurement inbox). Buyer accepts.
- Seller requests activation from Marketplace Finance to map buyer PO number to the offer (this is the manual step if you want an invoice that references your PO).
- Marketplace Finance completes entitlement activation (usually same-day) or within 1–3 business days depending on backlog. If manual invoice mapping is needed it's 3–5 business days.

Evidence we can attach to your procurement request: SOC2 Type II (redacted), subprocessor register, data residency statement, and a short SSO/SCIM integration note if you need automated user provisioning.

If you want an example mapping, see attachment (activation_flow.svg) — this shows the timeboxes. If Medicorps needs to keep invoicing to AP on a single annual invoice, we recommend the billed-commitment approach; it avoids per-usage billing spikes and maps cleanly to PO lines.

Finally — for expedited activation (to hit Jun 10 pilot) we can prioritize your deal if you confirm by Friday and provide the internal PO number. Happy to join the call Wednesday.

—Ben Carter
Seller Operations
Redwood Inference
(attachment: activation_flow.svg)

Aisha, Ben —

Thanks, that helps. Our internal cutover window is tight — pilot must start June 10 and procurement needs the full evidence pack + a sample invoice showing PO reference. I've attached an internal licensing summary (Medico_Licensing_Summary.xlsx) to show what we currently bill as an annual line item.

On Wednesday 10:00am PT works. We'll have: myself, our AP lead (Sofia), and our cloud platform manager (Marcus). Items for the call:
- Walk through the billed-commitment option and confirm sample invoice layout
- Confirm evidence pack contents and signature authority required
- Get rough ETA for activation once buyer accepts the offer

Also: is there any reason we should involve AWS Marketplace support directly at this stage? Happy to loop them if helpful.

Regards,
Alex

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@medicorps.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Jun 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Converting existing license to AWS Private Offer — approvals, billing, and evidence

Alex —

Thanks for pulling the team together on Wednesday. Quick note following our call and the internal approvals you outlined:

1) We will prepare a billed-commitment private offer that mirrors your annual PO. That means a single invoice referencing your PO number; Finance will accept the PO mapping.

2) Evidence pack: we will produce a single ZIP with SOC 2 Type II, subprocessor list, data residency statement, and a short SSO/SCIM doc. Aisha will attach the full bundle to the private offer.

3) Timelines: with your PO number and signed acceptance by Friday, Marketplace activation should land by next Wednesday (3 business days). If your AP requires the invoice to be issued before provisioning, allow an additional 1 business day for accounting mapping.

4) Commercial gesture: for a 12-month committed private offer we can apply a 7% implementation credit off list price (applied as a one-time invoice credit post-activation). If that helps speed internal approvals, we can include it in the offer.

Next steps (clear asks):
- Alex: share the PO number and the preferred DocuSign signatory (name + email).
- Medicorps: confirm acceptance of the 12-month committed model and the 7% credit (opt-in).
- Redwood: draft private offer + DocuSign SOW and attach evidence bundle.

I'll create the DocuSign packet and share a link once we have signatory details. If you'd like AWS Marketplace support involved, I can CC them into the activation request but we rarely need direct AWS intervention for standard billed-commitment flows.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Medicorps live for the June 10 pilot.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sales Lead, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
